title: Effective etale descent for finite etale morphisms
statement: Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] (for instance $Y'=\coprod_iY_i$ for an etale covering $\{Y_i\to Y\}$), and put $Y''=Y'\times_YY'$, $Y'''=Y'\times_YY'\times_YY'$ (fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]) with projections $p_1,p_2:Y''\to Y'$ and $p_{12},p_{13},p_{23}:Y'''\to Y''$. Let $\mathsf{DD}$ be the category whose objects are pairs $(P',\varphi)$ of a finite etale $Y'$-scheme $P'$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] and a descent datum on $P'$ over $Y'/Y$ [def-pd-descent-datum], i.e. an isomorphism $\varphi:p_1^*P'\cong p_2^*P'$ of schemes over $Y''$ satisfying $p_{13}^*\varphi=p_{23}^*\varphi\circ p_{12}^*\varphi$ over $Y'''$, and whose morphisms $(P',\varphi)\to(Q',\chi)$ are the $Y'$-morphisms $\beta:P'\to Q'$ with $\chi\circ p_1^*\beta=p_2^*\beta\circ\varphi$. For a finite etale $Y$-scheme $P$ let $\mathrm{can}_P:p_1^*(P\times_YY')\to p_2^*(P\times_YY')$ be the composite of the canonical isomorphisms of both sides with $P\times_YY''$ (they exist since $g\circ p_1=g\circ p_2$). Then the functor $\mathsf{FEt}(Y)\to\mathsf{DD}$, $P\mapsto(P\times_YY',\mathrm{can}_P)$, $\alpha\mapsto\alpha\times_YY'$, is an equivalence of categories: the category of finite etale $Y$-schemes is equivalent to the category of finite etale $Y'$-schemes endowed with a descent datum.

proof.text: Step 1 ($\{g\}$ is an fpqc covering). Since $g$ is etale, $(Y',g)$ is an object of the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]; since $g$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], the one-member family $\{g:Y'\to Y\}$ is jointly surjective, hence a covering family of $Y$ in $Y_{\Et}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] it is an fpqc covering of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

source.place: Topologies, Lemma Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc, line 3044): an etale covering is an fpqc covering

proof.text: Step 2 (the functor). For $P\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$, $P'=P\times_YY'$ is a finite etale $Y'$-scheme and $\alpha\mapsto\alpha\times_YY'$ is the base change functor $g^*:\mathsf{FEt}(Y)\to\mathsf{FEt}(Y')$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. By the universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $p_k^*P'=(P\times_YY')\times_{Y',p_k}Y''$ is canonically isomorphic to $P\times_YY''$ over $Y''$ for $k=1,2$, because $g\circ p_1=g\circ p_2$; so $\mathrm{can}_P$ is an isomorphism over $Y''$. Pulled back along $p_{12},p_{13},p_{23}$, each of the three isomorphisms becomes the composite of the canonical identifications with $P\times_YY'''$, so $p_{13}^*\mathrm{can}_P=p_{23}^*\mathrm{can}_P\circ p_{12}^*\mathrm{can}_P$: $(P',\mathrm{can}_P)$ is a descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum]. For a $Y$-morphism $\alpha:P\to Q$, both $\mathrm{can}_Q\circ p_1^*(\alpha\times_YY')$ and $p_2^*(\alpha\times_YY')\circ\mathrm{can}_P$ correspond under these identifications to $\alpha\times_YY''$, so $\alpha\times_YY'$ is a morphism of $\mathsf{DD}$; functoriality is that of $g^*$.

source.place: Descent, Definition Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum, line 8101) and Remark 'remark-easier' (pr_0^*V -> pr_1^*V, cocycle pr_02^* = pr_12^* o pr_01^*); the canonical datum on a base change

proof.text: Step 3 (fully faithful). Morphisms in $\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$ are all $Y$-morphisms, and morphisms in $\mathsf{DD}$ are all $Y'$-morphisms compatible with the data. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend] to the fpqc covering $\{g:Y'\to Y\}$ of Step 1 (with $S=Y$, $X=Y'$, $X_2=Y''$, $\mathrm{pr}_0=p_1$, $\mathrm{pr}_1=p_2$) and to $U=P$, $W=Q$ for $P,Q\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$: the map $\alpha\mapsto\alpha\times_YY'$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P,Q)$ onto the $Y'$-morphisms $\beta:P\times_YY'\to Q\times_YY'$ with $\mathrm{can}_Q\circ p_1^*\beta=p_2^*\beta\circ\mathrm{can}_P$, which is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{DD}}((P\times_YY',\mathrm{can}_P),(Q\times_YY',\mathrm{can}_Q))$. So the functor of Step 2 is fully faithful.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02W0 (lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful, line 8858), last sentence

proof.text: Step 4 (effectivity). Let $(P',\varphi)\in\mathsf{DD}$. The morphism $P'\to Y'$ is finite, hence affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], since a finite morphism is by definition affine with finite ring maps over affine opens [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. By [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective], applied to the fpqc covering $\{g:Y'\to Y\}$ of Step 1 and to $V=P'$ with the descent datum $\varphi$, there are a scheme $P$ with a morphism $P\to Y$ and an isomorphism $\psi:P\times_YY'\to P'$ of $Y'$-schemes with $\varphi\circ p_1^*\psi=p_2^*\psi\circ\mathrm{can}_P$.

Step 5 ($P$ is finite etale over $Y$). The base change $P\times_YY'\to Y'$ of $P\to Y$ along $g$ is the composite of the isomorphism $\psi$ with the finite etale $P'\to Y'$. It is finite: the preimage of an affine open $W\subseteq Y'$ is $\psi^{-1}$ of its (affine) preimage in $P'$, with the same ring map up to the isomorphism $\psi^\sharp$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; and it is etale, since flatness, unramifiedness and local finite presentation are read on local rings and affine charts, which $\psi$ identifies [def-weil-etale-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] for the fpqc covering $\{g\}$ (one index), $P\to Y$ is finite; by [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] for the same covering, $P\to Y$ is etale. So $P\in\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and by Step 4 $\psi$ is an isomorphism $(P\times_YY',\mathrm{can}_P)\cong(P',\varphi)$ in $\mathsf{DD}$ (its inverse is compatible because $\psi$ is). Hence the functor of Step 2 is essentially surjective.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02LA (lemma-descending-property-finite, line 6102) and Lemma Tag 02VN (lemma-descending-property-etale, line 6209), direction '<=' of Definition Tag 02KO (line 5310)

proof.text: Step 6 (equivalence). A functor that is fully faithful (Step 3) and essentially surjective (Step 5) is an equivalence of categories: choosing for each object $(P',\varphi)$ of $\mathsf{DD}$ a $P$ and an isomorphism $\psi$ as in Steps 4-5 defines on objects a quasi-inverse, which full faithfulness makes a functor with the $\psi$ as natural isomorphisms.
